pr_title: syncutil: make IntMap generic, rename to Map
pr_body:
Closes #103147.

Will help #120597, so that it does not need to use the interface-heavy stdlib `sync.`Map just because its key is not an `int64`.

This PR makes `syncutil.IntMap` (renamed to `syncutil.Map`) generic, so that it can be used with keys other than `int64`. This restores some of the generality lost when the standard library's `sync.Map` was specialized in our `IntMap` fork in 8340120c. It does so without losing the performance benefits that specialization provided, because we use generics instead of interface objects. This limited use of generics with no virtual function calls performs identically to the hand-specialized version.

The use of generics also provides type safety. Callers no longer need to cast int-like keys to and from `int64`. They also no longer need to cast typed-pointers to and from `unsafe.Pointer`.

Would be nice to make this generic, unless there's already a good/better implementation upstream. It might hamper performance though, since it prevents some compiler optimizations.

Jira issue: CRDB-27851

Something like:

```
./dev bench ./pkg/util/syncutil --count 10 --timeout 10m -v | grep Benchmark > bench-old.txt
```

Then do the same for `bench-new.txt` and run `benchstat bench-old.txt bench-new.txt`.

Oh, and you'll want to keep the benchmark names the same with the old/new implementation, so that `benchstat` can compare the before/after. Either by renaming the benchmarks, or by processing the raw benchmark results.
